known.title: The plan says that `bun install --frozen-lockfile` runs the claude-code `postinstall`, but this repository denies every dependency lifecycle script.
known.summary: The fact says that `claude plugin validate` gets the lockfile-pinned CLI because `bun install --frozen-lockfile` runs the package's `postinstall`. At repo_ref, `package.json:18` sets `"trustedDependencies": []`, and the Bun documentation (https://bun.com/docs/pm/lifecycle, section "Behavior of the trustedDependencies field") says that `trustedDependencies: []` allows no packages to run lifecycle scripts, including the default list. That is why `.github/workflows/ci.yml:135-138` runs `node node_modules/@anthropic-ai/claude-code/install.cjs` after the install (step name "trustedDependencies denies it by default"), and `.github/AGENTS.md:108-109` gives the same reason. The `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` 2.1.234 package has `"postinstall": "node install.cjs"` and ships a placeholder `bin/claude.exe` that prints `Error: claude native binary not installed.` until that script runs. Effect: an implementer who follows the fact skips `install.cjs`, so `scripts/ci.mjs:398-403` reports `claude plugin validate` as failed and A1 cannot exit 0 (or a different, unpinned `claude` on `PATH` validates the plugin).

known.title: Acceptance A3 searches for a phrase that crosses a line break, so it passes on the unfixed step 11.
known.summary: A3 runs `grep -n 'then archive and run Teardown'` and expects no output and exit 1. At repo_ref, `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/yolo/SKILL.md:307` ends with `then` and line 308 starts with `archive and run Teardown.`, so the phrase is split across two lines. grep matches one line at a time and cannot match a newline (GNU grep manual, https://www.gnu.org/software/grep/manual/grep.html: "there is no way to match newline characters in a text"; exit status 1 when no lines are selected). `git show <repo_ref>:plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/yolo/SKILL.md | grep -n 'then archive and run Teardown'` prints nothing and exits 1 on the unchanged file, while `grep -n 'archive and run Teardown'` matches line 308. Effect: A3 passes before step 1 runs and cannot show that the archive call left step 11; it is the only command check for the Done when clause "it no longer says to archive on its own".

known.title: Steps 1 and 2 list the same file, but step 2 has no Depends on step 1, which the plan contract forbids.
known.locator: Steps, row 2 refresh_hash, Depends cell (line 39); Steps, row 1 fix_step_11 (line 38)
known.summary: Both rows list `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/yolo/SKILL.md` in Files, and both now have Depends `-`. `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/plan-manager/references/plan-contract.md:73-74` at repo_ref says: "Two steps that list the same path need a Depends chain between them, or one of them must own the shared edit." Lines 241-242 add that the helper prints advice for two steps that share a Files path with no Depends chain, and line 99 says to finish dependencies before dependent work. Effect: the content-hash backfill can run before or in parallel with the prose edit. Step 2's Done when (`--check-only` exits 0) is then true on the unchanged file, and the later meaning change in step 1 leaves `content_hash` and `metadata.updated` stale, which `plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/AGENTS.md:23-31` requires to be refreshed after the meaning change.

known.title: Step 1 falls back to step 10 when step 9 fails, but after the merge step 10 cannot leave the pull request and issue open.
known.summary: The Task makes new step 11 say "on `Merge now`, follow step 9, or step 10 when step 9 fails". At repo_ref, step 9 (`plugins/plan-lifecycle/skills/productivity/yolo/SKILL.md:300-302`) merges first and then archives and runs Teardown; the merge cannot be undone. The pull request body ends with `Closes #<n>` (line 284), and GitHub closes the linked issue when the pull request merges into the default branch (https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue). So when `archive` or Teardown fails after the merge, step 10 (lines 303-305: leave the pull request and the issue open, run Teardown's exit without a merge) cannot happen: the pull request is merged and the issue is closed. The contract keeps the exit without a merge for a plan that stops without the landing merge (`plan-contract.md:422-428`), runs `archive` after the landing merge (line 369) and the After archive teardown (lines 401-420), and gives a retry procedure for a short-lived helper failure (lines 293-301). Effect: the run treats step 9 as all-or-nothing, leaves a merged plan without archive (stale phase labels), keeps the merged branch and worktree, reports the wrong state, and starts the new run.
